relevance_note: Case report of two Croatian brothers with familial LCAT deficiency and their carrier parents: 'the proband was compound heterozygous for two novel LCAT variants'.
method_note: Read in full and built by a short Python script from my reading; every span checked verbatim (variant spans contain no-break spaces as in the paper). Labels: the paper gives no own labels ('Proband', 'Brother', 'Father', 'Mother' are role words); there are two patients, so rule 5 does not apply; Table 2 shows the family as columns (header row: Proband | Brother | Father | Mother), so the proband is 'Table 2 column 1' and relatives follow rule 2 ('brother of', 'father of', 'mother of'). Table 1 is the proband at admission; Table 2 is a following visit (values differ, e.g. total cholesterol 8.3 vs 4.70, HDL 0.42 vs 0.23, triglycerides 16.58 vs 7.36). The brother's HDL is 0.24 mmol/L and triglycerides 4.28 mmol/l in the text but 0.22 and 1.85 in Table 2 (probably different time points; both recorded in severity_or_detail). Table-value features (low apoA-I/A-II, low apoB, elevated unesterified cholesterol, low ferritin, low C3, parents' HDL/triglycerides) were judged against the reference values printed in the same table row; values within the reference range were not used to exclude anything (no text calls them normal). Reduced cholesteryl ester fraction is recorded from the stated 'increased unesterified to total cholesterol ratio' (proband) and the unesterified/total row of Table 2 (brother). Hematuria for the proband is from 3–7 erythrocytes in urine sediment against reference 0–2. Possible tension: the father 'had no other signs of the disease' apart from low HDL, yet Table 2 gives triglycerides 2.7 mmol/L (reference <1.71); the mother 'was healthy' yet HDL 0.91 mmol/L (reference >1). Both table values recorded as observed; the broad statements excluded nothing specific ('other signs of the disease' kept as a separate excluded row for the father; 'healthy' not turned into a feature row). Membranous nephropathy (diagnosed at age 19) is recorded as stated; the authors later attribute the renal disease to LCAT deficiency. Age at onset left not reported (19 is an age at a prior diagnosis, not stated as symptom onset). Age at last evaluation for the proband is his age at admission (30); later events (hemodialysis 4 years later) have no stated age. Kidney histology (Fig. 1, Fig. 2) is assigned to the proband per the text; for the brother the paper says only that a biopsy confirmed the diagnosis. Brother's variants: the paper says the brothers carry 'the same genetic variants'; zygosity and inheritance left not reported for him (not stated for him). Pathogenicity ('novel pathogenetic') recorded for the two brothers only. No protein HGVS printed (only 'Alanine 166 with a Threonine', 'Arginine to Cysteine at the codon 380'), so protein_hgvs null. Transcript NM_000229 is from the Methods. The brother's red blood cell count 'within the lower normal range' recorded as low red blood cell count excluded; checklist anemia left not reported (haemoglobin not given).

span: was unsuccessfully treated with immunosuppressive agents (steroids, cyclophosphamide, cyclosporine)
The proband was treated with diuretics, antihypertensives, iron supplements, and erythropoietin. Patient has never taken lipid-lowering drugs.
His renal function declined gradually and 4 years later (15 years after initial presentation) he started with regular hemodialysis sessions.
Although initially combined kidney and split liver transplantation was considered, we opted for kidney transplantation only
